title: If no AC brightness value has been configured, switching from low battery mode to AC power should restore previous screen brightness
line: Plugging the charger back in after Low Battery dimmed the screen now brings the brightness back to where it was, unless AC has its own brightness set.
explanation: PowerDevil applies a profile's brightness when switching to it, and only lowers it when going to a more conservative profile (Battery, Low Battery). When the next profile has no brightness setting of its own (AC by default), the brightness action isn't loaded for it, so nothing ever undid the reduction and the screen stayed at the Low Battery level after plugging in. The action now remembers each internal display's brightness from before the first reduction and, once the system is back on that profile or a less conservative one without its own brightness, sets it back. It forgets the value if the user (or anything else) changes the brightness in the meantime, and a profile with its own configured brightness still wins.

commits.message:
screenbrightnesscontrol: restore brightness when leaving a dimmer profile

Switching to Low Battery reduced the brightness, but plugging AC back in
left it there unless AC had its own brightness set. Remember the earlier
brightness and restore it, unless the user changed it in the meantime.

BUG: 484663

media.caption: Master: at 80% on AC, Low Battery dims to 30%, and plugging AC back in leaves it at 30%.
With the fix: 80% on AC, 30% on Low Battery, back to 80% when AC is plugged in.
Master, AC / Low Battery / AC again: 80%, 30%, 30%.
With the fix, AC / Low Battery / AC again: 80%, 30%, 80%.
